answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a refundable berth bond. Every new identity must lock real funds before it may act, as a boat pays before entering an inlet. Throwaway identities turn unprofitable: an attacker running ten thousand accounts must post ten thousand bonds in capital. Accounts caught in a correlated cluster - shared funding or behaviour - are slashed and evicted from the jetty, so duplicates forfeit their stake. Honest agents reclaim the bond on exit. A lantern on the ledger marks each bonded actor, and peers refuse to trade with anything unlit.
